neighbours.label: having time or slack to spare (no rush): the tokens that state an available time margin ('so I have time', 'the luxury of time', 'years left'), versus the same constructions under time pressure or about non-time things
fire: The train doesn't leave until noon, so we have time for breakfast.
Retired now, she has all the time in the world for her garden.
The exam is next month, so I still have weeks to prepare.
At current rates there are decades of oil left in the field.
Our flight was delayed, which gave us plenty of time to shop.
He finished early and had an hour to spare before the meeting.
With the deadline moved to spring, the team has months remaining.
There is no rush; you have until Friday to reply.
quiet: The train leaves in five minutes, so we must skip breakfast.
Retired now, she has a small house with a pretty garden.
The exam is in an hour, so I must stop reading and go.
At current rates there are dozens of rigs in the field.
Our flight was cancelled, which gave us a voucher for the shop.
He finished late and ran straight into the meeting.
With the deadline moved to today, the team is panicking.
There is a problem; you have a broken link in the reply.
